#1 · This does not escape backslash characters in the input.
The code only escapes spaces with backslashes but does not escape existing backslashes in filenames. An attacker
could create a file named 'foo\\ bar' which becomes 'foo\\\\ bar' after replacement, potentially allowing argument
injection when the path is interpolated into a shell command. The stdout comes from a find command scanning the

#2 · This does not escape backslash characters in the input.
Same vulnerability as finding 4 but in a different code path (split by '\n' instead of os.EOL). The replacement only
handles spaces, leaving backslashes unescaped. If these paths are used in shell command construction, an
attacker-controlled filename with backslashes could break argument boundaries.
